title: A novel meta-heuristic search algorithm for solving optimization problems: capuchin search algorithm

title: Pirates Swarm Search Algorithm: A Meta-Heuristic Search Algorithm for optimization problems
abstract: Abstract In this study, we have suggested a meta-heuristic algorithm based on swarm intelligence for single-objective optimization problems. Our inspiration comes from historical and behavioral fashions of pirates at 1600s and 1700s which also is known as the golden age of piracy. They navigate in the oceans to find treasures and we search the problem space to find a better solution. Triangle trade is the search space and each pirate ship is a search agent. A bunch of well-known benchmark functions are used to run some qualitative, quantitative and statistically tests to see the outcome of the suggested algorithm. Obtained results shows that the algorithm is able to explore and exploit in search space as expected and also has the ability of improving the average fitness of population and improving the best so far solution. At the end; results of suggested algorithm comparing to other well-known ones such as Particle Swarm Optimization, Gravity Search Algorithm, Ranking Genetic Algorithm and Sparrow search algorithm shows that it is able to outperform these algorithms in most of the studied cases.

title: Damped Oscillation Search (DOS): A Novel Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: An innovative and physically-inspired, non-gradient algorithm was created in the current paper as a solution to global optimization issues. Because it is imitated by the damped harmonic oscillation of a physical pendulum, the new algorithm is termed Damped Oscillation Search (DOS) algorithm. It comprises a primary solution search (PSS), which updates the pivot point with the moment of inertia, and a secondary solution search (SSS), which improves the pivot point with the damped amplitude oscillation; the optimal solution was allocated into two functions. Evaluated against previous standards from two batches of continuous test problems, sixteen standardized benchmark mathematics functions, and six benchmark constraint engineering problems, as described in a number of previously reported tests and studies published in various sources. Testing and analysis were then carried out for the DOS algorithm. The recommended technique is favorably competed with other recognized efficiency meta-heuristics, as supported by the current study results. Additionally, the current paper discussed the features employed in the DOS algorithm, which were analyzed regarding prospective consequences for actual constrained engineering optimization issues.
